findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm against the installed pydantic-ai 1.107.9 that `AnthropicModelSettings.anthropic_effort` exists and copies into `output_config.effort` (and that the cited `anthropic.py:1960-1978` / `bedrock.py:338,706` seams match that build), and have `test_settings_builders_seam.py` assert the exact wire field so a renamed/dropped setting fails loudly.
evidence: Plan: "`anthropic_effort` on direct Anthropic, which `AnthropicModel` copies into `output_config.effort` unconditionally (`pydantic_ai/models/anthropic.py:1960-1978`...)"
resolve_symbol: `AnthropicModelSettings` EXISTS; `anthropic_effort` UNRESOLVED (not proof of absence)
Retrieved docs confirm Anthropic `output_config.effort` (default high) and pydantic-ai Anthropic-scoped settings pattern, but do not name `anthropic_effort` at the cited lines
pyproject.toml:133 pins `pydantic-ai-slim[...]>=1.107,<2`, consistent with the cited 1.107.9
findings.finding: The 'Effort, explicit' mechanism depends entirely on pydantic-ai 1.107.9 exposing an `anthropic_effort` provider-scoped setting (cited at `anthropic.py:1960-1978`) that copies into `output_config.effort`, and on `bedrock_additional_model_requests_fields` being merged (`bedrock.py:338/706`). Web docs corroborate the Anthropic `output_config.effort` API and that pydantic-ai has analogous Anthropic-scoped settings (anthropic_cache, task_budget), but the exact `anthropic_effort` setting name and those line references are the one unverified capability assertion in the plan; if the installed build instead routes effort through a generic passthrough (e.g. extra output_config fields) the named setting would be a no-op.
scenarios: pydantic-ai 1.107.9 names the setting differently or gates it behind a profile flag, so pinned `high`/`medium` is silently dropped and 5.5 models run at API-default effort

findings.checklist_item: State how build_model_settings selects the effort settings key per provider (e.g. set BOTH `anthropic_effort` and the bedrock additional-fields key and rely on each model class to ignore the foreign key, or thread a provider/endpoint signal into the builder) given it currently has no provider branch.
evidence: Plan: "structured_run.build_model_settings sends it ... through pydantic-ai 1.107.9's provider-scoped settings: anthropic_effort on direct Anthropic ... and bedrock_additional_model_requests_fields=... on Bedrock"
structured_run.py:363-366: "this is a capability check, never a provider-name branch" — build_model_settings takes `resolved` (a str) and `caps`, no provider/endpoint argument
No effort/anthropic_effort/bedrock_additional_model_requests_fields key is set anywhere under src/rebar/llm today (searched)
findings.finding: The effort-delivery mechanism does not specify how `build_model_settings` chooses the provider-specific settings key. The plan requires `anthropic_effort` on direct Anthropic and `bedrock_additional_model_requests_fields={"output_config": {"effort": ...}}` on Bedrock, but the builder is deliberately 'a capability check, never a provider-name branch' and receives only the resolved model-id string, with no provider/endpoint signal.
scenarios: A Bedrock 5.5 run where the builder emits `anthropic_effort` (silently ignored by BedrockModel) and never populates the bedrock additional-fields key — effort is lost and Opus/Haiku default to `medium`, the regression the plan set out to prevent
A direct Anthropic run where only the bedrock key is set
findings.suggested_fix: Specify that the builder emits both provider-scoped keys unconditionally (each pydantic-ai model class drops the key it doesn't recognize), or that the effort value is threaded via a provider-aware wrapper so only the matching key is set; add a settings-builder-seam test asserting the correct key appears for a Bedrock resolved id and for a direct id.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the effort table's key-matching rule — either bare-family substring match (so `us.`/`global.` Bedrock ids resolve) or explicit rows for all three id forms as the sampling override does — and assert it in the Bedrock happy-path effort test.
evidence: Plan: “a per-model table pins `high` for Opus and Sonnet 5.5… structured_run.build_model_settings sends it… bedrock_additional_model_requests_fields={"output_config": {"effort": ...}} on Bedrock”

Contrast: the sibling sampling change is explicit about id forms — “Add each 5.5 id (bare, `us.`, `global.`) to `_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES`…” (capabilities.py:223), confirmed to carry separate `us.`/`global.` rows for Opus 4.7/4.8
Bedrock requests resolve to `us.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5` (the ids the plan itself lists), so a bare-only key would miss the Bedrock arm

Existing substring tables (MODEL_WINDOW_LADDER model_classes.py:62, MODEL_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS verify.py:294) use bare family names matched by containment, which WOULD match `us.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5`; the plan does not state the effort table follows this convention
findings.finding: The new per-model effort table that pins `high` for Opus/Sonnet 5.5 does not specify its key-matching rule (bare family substring vs. exact qualified ids), so it is undefined whether a resolved Bedrock id (`us.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5`) matches and receives `high`.
scenarios: Deploy to Bedrock (896586841071/us-east-1) where every frontier/standard call resolves a `us.anthropic.*` id
A Bedrock Opus 5.5 call that should run at pinned `high` instead silently rides the API default
findings.suggested_fix: State that the effort table is substring-matched on bare family names (mirroring MODEL_WINDOW_LADDER / MODEL_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS) so `us.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5` and `global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5` both resolve to `high`; alternatively enumerate bare, `us.`, and `global.` keys as _MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES does.

findings.checklist_item: State that BOTH own_window_tokens (model_classes.py) and largest_window_tokens (sizing.py) consult PRIOR_GENERATION_WINDOWS before their unlocated floor, and cover a pinned-4.x window via the sizing accessor in the edge test.
evidence: Plan: "the 4.x windows move to PRIOR_GENERATION_WINDOWS, consulted before the 200K unlocated floor, so Sonnet 4.6 keeps 1M"
model_classes.py:78-84 own_window_tokens falls back to ladder_min when the model is not located in MODEL_WINDOW_LADDER
sizing.py:78 largest_window_tokens independently falls back to `min(w for _, w in MODEL_LADDER)` for an unlocated model — a distinct code path from own_window_tokens
findings.finding: The plan localizes the PRIOR_GENERATION_WINDOWS lookup to the 'unlocated 200K floor' path only, but two separate accessors fall back on that floor: own_window_tokens (model_classes.py:78-84) and largest_window_tokens (sizing.py:57-79), the latter being the P8 escalation-budget consumer with its own `min(w for _, w in MODEL_LADDER)` miss fallback. The plan does not say both consult PRIOR_GENERATION_WINDOWS.
scenarios: A run pinned to Sonnet 4.6 (now absent from the 5.5-only MODEL_WINDOW_LADDER): own_window_tokens honors PRIOR_GENERATION_WINDOWS and returns 1M, but largest_window_tokens still hits its ladder MIN (200K), so P8 over-blocks / mis-sizes chunks for the pinned prior-gen model
findings.suggested_fix: Make PRIOR_GENERATION_WINDOWS a shared lookup both accessors call before returning the ladder MIN, and add an edge test asserting largest_window_tokens('...claude-sonnet-4-6') == 1_000_000.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the failure-disposition contract for a 5.5 content_filter / `refusal` stop reason: the explicit disposition (retryable/transient vs fatal/permanent) the caller surfaces, and — for the code-review-failover chain — which arm's disposition wins when the fallback itself declines.
evidence: 'Bedrock Opus 5.5 declines (content_filtered) any request whose output schema asks for reasoning in the response'
'Walk every model call site ... against the five changes plus the `refusal` stop reason'

The remedy named is neutral wording to stop the filter firing; no disposition word (retryable vs fatal) is stated for a content_filter/refusal that still occurs, and the failover arm is named but its fallback-failure winner is not.
findings.finding: The cutover introduces a new reachable failure mode on 5.5 — Bedrock Opus 5.5 returns content_filtered / a `refusal` stop reason — and the plan audits it but never states its disposition contract: whether a content_filter/refusal on the code-review-failover arm surfaces as retryable/transient or fatal/permanent to the caller.
findings.location: Approach — 'Reasoning-in-output wording' and 'Audit' (the `refusal` stop reason; 'code-review-failover declined 3 of 3')
scenarios: After the wording fix a residual content_filtered/refusal still occurs in prod; if it is classified fatal it masks an otherwise retryable condition, or if silently swallowed it yields a wrong green.
On the code-review-failover path, a content_filter decline on the primary vs the fallback arm — the plan does not say which disposition wins.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the rollback/back-out for the production model cutover (e.g. the id swap + compose + terraform are a single revertable commit, so back-out = revert that commit and redeploy), confirming the before-run 4.x configuration is the known-good restore target.

'provider-parity probe and full run once on 4.x before the change and once on 5.5 after' records state but is not a back-out
ABSENCE: no AC or approach sentence names how to revert the cutover if the 5.5 run regresses
findings.finding: The plan performs a production model cutover (DEFAULT_MODEL, compose deploy slots at docker-compose.yml:97-99, and terraform alarm ModelId dimensions at monitoring_eb6e.tf:80-135) in one commit, but states no explicit rollback / back-out plan if 5.5 misbehaves in production after deploy. T4 requires the reversibility mechanism, not just before/after recording.
findings.location: Approach ('The deploy defaults ... change in the same commit') + Acceptance Criteria
scenarios: 5.5 Opus returns worse verdicts or new refusal patterns in production and operators need to return to 4.x quickly
A terraform alarm/compose mismatch is only caught post-deploy
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to Approach that the id swap, compose slots, and terraform alarm dimensions ship as one atomic, revertable commit whose revert restores the measured-good 4.x configuration, and note who redeploys on regression.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the rollout/rollback story: either stage the 5.5 cutover (canary / per-slot flip) or document an explicit, tested revert (restore the 4.x ids in toml/compose/terraform and redeploy), and note whether old+new ids coexist during the change.
evidence: 'The deploy defaults in infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:97-99 and the alarm ModelId dimensions in infra/terraform/monitoring_eb6e.tf:80-135 change in the same commit'
'The epic lands this first, on the current engine.'
No AC or Approach text names a flag/canary/staged rollout or a rollback procedure; the only post-deploy item cited is the sibling metric check itchy-neutral-whooper.
findings.finding: The cutover flips production model ids for all traffic in a single commit (compose deploy defaults + terraform alarm ModelId dimensions + toml ids change together) with no flag, canary, or staged rollout, and the plan states no explicit, cheap, tested rollback path to revert to 4.x if 5.5 misbehaves in prod.
findings.location: Approach — 'The deploy defaults in infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:97-99 and the alarm ModelId dimensions ... change in the same commit'; Acceptance Criteria
scenarios: 5.5 behaves worse than 4.x in production (regressions in review quality, unexpected content_filter declines, or Bedrock metric gaps) and operators have no stated quick revert.
A single-commit flip means old+new do not coexist; if a rollback is needed it is an ad-hoc git revert + redeploy with no tested procedure.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Rollout/Rollback subsection: e.g. revert = re-pin the three 4.x ids in rebar.toml + the two provider tomls + compose + alarms and redeploy (config-only, no data cleanup); optionally flip one slot/model first and verify provider-parity before the rest.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Prove the direct-Anthropic effort path end-to-end through pydantic-ai 1.107.9 (emit `anthropic_effort` and assert the outbound request carries `output_config.effort` for an unlisted 5.5 id), not just that the raw SDK accepts output_config.effort.
evidence: Plan: 'The wire behaviour was probed … direct Anthropic (SDK) … effort (… direct output_config.effort) is accepted' — the probe used output_config.effort directly, not anthropic_effort via pydantic-ai.
Plan: 'pydantic-ai-slim 1.107.9's profile does not list 5.5 ids.'
Confirmed no `anthropic_effort` key exists anywhere under src/rebar/llm (search: no matches), so this is a first-time use of that settings surface.
AnthropicModelSettings resolves EXISTS, but the specific `anthropic_effort` → output_config.effort copy behavior is PARTIALLY-VERIFIED (cannot read .venv source to confirm the cited lines).
findings.finding: The direct-Anthropic effort delivery is asserted from a pydantic-ai source reading but not exercised end-to-end: the 2026-11-09 probe set `output_config.effort` on the raw Anthropic SDK, whereas rebar will emit `anthropic_effort` through pydantic-ai 1.107.9, whose profile the plan itself says does not list the 5.5 ids. The claim that `AnthropicModel` copies `anthropic_effort` into `output_config.effort` unconditionally (profile flag only gates the thinking-derived fallback) is the load-bearing step and rests solely on cited source lines, not a probe through rebar's actual transport.
scenarios: pydantic-ai 1.107.9 gates the output_config.effort emission on a profile flag that the unlisted 5.5 id does not set, so effort is silently dropped on direct Anthropic and Opus/Sonnet 5.5 run at default depth instead of the pinned `high`.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a settings-builder-seam assertion (or a one-shot captured-request live probe) that a built direct-Anthropic model_settings with `anthropic_effort` actually serializes `output_config.effort` on a 5.5 id under pydantic-ai 1.107.9, closing the gap between the raw-SDK probe and rebar's transport.
